head: f5bef37
target: AGENTS.md sets the contributor rules that keep the one plugin tree working across Claude Code, Factory Droid, and Codex: one shared copy of the manifest and hooks, hook scripts find the plugin root from their own path and never from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, and editing hooks.json breaks Codex trust.
incidental: README documents the install, opt-in, and update flows the code already has; the author owned those designs when the code was built.
CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md so Claude Code reads the same rules.
Steps a contributor runs, which AGENTS.md states as rules: scripts/selftest, claude plugin validate, and the plugin.json version bump.
The per-harness install and update commands in README.

questions.prompt: Why does the repo keep one copy of .claude-plugin/ and hooks/hooks.json instead of one per harness?

options.label: All three harnesses read the same layout, so one copy makes a change land once everywhere and stops the three copies from drifting apart.
Only one harness can own the git pre-push hook, so the plugin tree must stay single.
Each harness needs its own copy so it can cache plugin updates independently.

key_points: all three harnesses read the same .claude-plugin/ and hooks/hooks.json layout
one copy means a change lands once for every harness
separate copies would drift and need the same change made three times

questions.prompt: A contributor edits hooks/session-start to read CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT from the environment instead of computing the plugin root from its own script path. What breaks?

options.label: In Factory Droid the variable holds a placeholder inside hook processes, so the hook no longer finds the skill's scripts.
Claude Code stops launching the hook, because hooks.json no longer matches the script.
Nothing breaks; CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT holds the plugin root in every harness.
Codex marks the hook untrusted and skips it.

key_points: Droid sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT to a placeholder inside hook processes
the hook resolves the wrong path and cannot find the skill scripts
the rule covers what hook scripts read at run time, not how hooks.json wires them

questions.prompt: What does Codex's trust check protect, and what does that cost this plugin?

options.label: It runs plugin hooks only after the user trusts their definition hash, so every hooks.json edit needs a codex-trust-hooks rerun.
It keeps untrusted commits out of the repo, so pushes stop until the quiz passes.
It stops the plugin from changing git settings, so every opt-in needs a fresh install.

key_points: Codex skips plugin hooks until their definition hash is trusted
the hash covers hooks.json content, so editing it invalidates trust on every Codex install
the failure is silent: the hooks just stop running in Codex
scripts/codex-trust-hooks writes the trust entries the Codex TUI would write on approval

questions.prompt: The plugin grows a new PreToolUse hook: a script under hooks/ plus its wiring in hooks/hooks.json. Which of these hold?

options.label: The new script must find the plugin root from its own path, never from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
The wiring in hooks.json may still use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, because the harness expands it when it launches the hook.
Codex users must rerun scripts/codex-trust-hooks after the change, because it edits hook definitions.
The wiring must be copied into a separate hooks file for each harness.

key_points: the rule applies to every hook script, because Droid puts a placeholder in the variable inside hook processes
hooks.json wiring may use the variable; the harness expands it before the hook runs
editing hooks.json changes Codex's trust hash, so Codex users must re-trust the hooks
one hooks.json serves all three harnesses, so the wiring lands once
